// diagnostic

E1318

`#Short("name")` is not a one-letter option `` or `` `#Short("n")` is used by both `first` and `second`

What

`#Short("name")` is not a one-letter option `` or `` `#Short("n")` is used by both `first` and `second`

Why

The shared command parser treats a short option as one ASCII letter, and each spelling must select only one `#CLI` field.

Fix

use one letter and give colliding fields different values.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E1318: tests/ui/cli_field_marker_misuse.stderr.

Error [E1319]: `#Short` has no CLI mapping for field `port`
  --> tests/ui/cli_field_marker_misuse.jet:2:6
    |
  2 |     #Short("p") port: Int
    |      ^^^^^
 Why: `#Short` and `#Env` describe generated command inputs, but this struct is not `#CLI`.
 Fix: remove the marker, or mark the command-input struct `#CLI`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1319

Error [E1318]: `#Short("port")` is not a one-letter option
  --> tests/ui/cli_field_marker_misuse.jet:7:6
    |
  7 |     #Short("port") port: Int
    |      ^^^^^
 Why: the shared command parser treats a short option as one ASCII letter.
 Fix: use one letter, such as `#Short("p")`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1318

Error [E1319]: `#Env` has no CLI mapping for field `verbose`
  --> tests/ui/cli_field_marker_misuse.jet:8:6
    |
  8 |     #Env("VERBOSE") verbose: Bool
    |      ^^^
 Why: a `Bool` command field is a presence flag, while `#Env` lowers to a value option.
 Fix: remove `#Env`, or use it on an `Int`, `Float`, `String`, `Path`, or optional value field
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1319
